items.title: OliveTin: Second-Order OS Command Injection via shellAfterCompleted
items.description:
Summary

OliveTin's shellAfterCompleted post-execution hook injects unsanitized variables — including arbitrary command output (output), the authenticated username (ot_username), and the exit code (exitCode) — directly into a shell command template processed by sh -c. Unlike the main action's argument handling, no checkShellArgumentSafety validation is applied to these variables. An attacker who can influence the output of a command (e.g., via user-supplied arguments that reflect in stdout, or through trusted-header username spoofing) can inject arbitrary OS commands into the post-execution shell.

This is a distinct finding from CVE-2026-27626 (OS command injection via password type in webhooks). That CVE addressed argument types bypassing shell safety checks in t

items.title: AIOHTTP: Unbounded buffering of data received during an upgrade request
items.description:
Summary

While a request flagged as an upgrade (e.g. a WebSocket handshake) was being handled, all further data received on the connection was buffered with no size limit or flow control until the handler completed.

Impact

An attacker could cause unbounded memory use by streaming data behind an upgrade request to any handler that does not immediately accept or reject the upgrade.

Patch: https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/3d850ee9b92573c7e913821cbcb96005beb3f4df
